stem: A nurse compares C-reactive protein (CRP) with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) for monitoring an inflammatory process. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: CRP generally rises and falls more rapidly than ESR as inflammatory activity changes.
options.B: CRP is specific for one diagnosis, whereas ESR is diagnostic of all inflammatory diseases.
options.C: ESR changes within minutes while CRP remains unchanged for weeks.
options.D: Neither test is affected by inflammation.

rationale: Both CRP and ESR are nonspecific inflammatory markers, but CRP changes more rapidly in response to inflammatory stimuli. CRP can rise within hours and decline promptly as the trigger resolves, whereas ESR typically rises more slowly and can remain elevated longer.
educational_objective: Differentiate the response kinetics of CRP and ESR.
source_document_title: Acute Inflammatory Response; C-Reactive Protein: Clinical Relevance and Interpretation
source_locator: CRP rises within hours and changes rapidly; ESR rises over approximately 24–48 hours and decreases more gradually
source_claim_supported: CRP generally responds more rapidly than ESR to changes in inflammatory activity; both markers are nonspecific.
correction_summary: Retained the valid comparison while removing claims that either marker identifies a specific diagnosis.
audit_findings: Correct kinetic distinction is directly supported.
Distractors incorrectly assign specificity or reverse kinetics.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
